skill.name: ru
skill.description: Repo Updater helps teams synchronize many GitHub repositories and coordinate AI-assisted review workflows from one CLI.
skill.summary: Synchronize multiple repositories and orchestrate AI-assisted review, dirty-repo cleanup, and release workflows.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline command names, XDG paths, and protective denylist entries. The main confirmed risks are the curl-to-bash installer and broad automation that can commit, push, tag, or release across repositories.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is documented as curl piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the one-line installer with download, checksum or signature verification, inspection, and then explicit execution steps.

remediation.issue: AI-assisted workflows can push changes, create tags, and publish releases.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before push, prune delete, force update, tag creation, or GitHub release operations.

remediation.issue: Agent-sweep can stage and commit files selected by automation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep denylist and secret scanning enabled by default, and require plan review before applying commits.

content.value_statement: Managing many repositories creates drift, stale branches, and missed review work. This skill guides Repo Updater workflows for syncing, auditing, and coordinating AI-assisted repository maintenance.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to sync many configured GitHub repositories with parallel workers.
Guides read-only repository status checks and JSON output workflows.
Describes AI-assisted review planning, application, and quality gates.
Documents agent-sweep workflows for repositories with uncommitted changes.
Shows configuration paths, repo list formats, and troubleshooting commands.
Explains ntm integration for managed Claude Code sessions.
limitations: Requires the separate Repo Updater CLI and its dependencies to be installed.
Write operations can commit, push, tag, or delete repositories when users enable those options.
GitHub operations depend on valid gh authentication and network access.
The skill is documentation-focused and does not include the full CLI implementation.

use_cases.title: Maintain many repositories
use_cases.description: Run planned sync and status workflows across personal, forked, or dependency repositories.

use_cases.title: Coordinate AI review work
use_cases.description: Plan and apply AI-assisted reviews while using worktrees, quality gates, and runtime budgets.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering leads and AI coding agent operators

use_cases.title: Clean dirty working trees
use_cases.description: Preview and process repositories with uncommitted changes using denylist and secret-scan guardrails.
use_cases.target_user: DevOps engineers maintaining shared project directories

prompt_templates.title: Check repository status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ru skill to explain how I can check the status of all configured repositories without modifying them.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a dry-run sync for my configured repositories, including JSON output and what warnings I should review first.

prompt_templates.title: Review AI-assisted changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through ru review --plan and ru review --apply, including quality gates and when pushing should require confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an agent sweep policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure an agent-sweep workflow for dirty repos with secret scanning, denylist rules, timeouts, and release controls.

output_examples.input: How do I safely sync all repos?
output_examples.output: Start with a dry run, inspect skipped and diverged repositories, then run a parallel sync only after confirming the update strategy.

output_examples.input: What should I check before agent-sweep?
output: Confirm the repo denylist covers secrets and build artifacts.
Use warn or block mode for secret scanning.
Review generated commit plans before applying them.

output_examples.input: Can this help with open PRs?
output_examples.output: Yes. It describes a review planning mode that queries GitHub issues and PRs, scores priorities, and prepares isolated worktrees.

best_practices: Run status and dry-run commands before any sync, prune, push, or release operation.
Keep secret scanning enabled and review denylist coverage before committing agent-selected files.
Use explicit runtime, repository, and parallelism limits for large multi-repo operations.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts into a shell without independent review.
Do not use force, delete, push, or release options without clear user confirmation.
Do not let automated agents stage files that match secret, credential, or build-artifact patterns.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users operate Repo Updater for multi-repository GitHub synchronization and AI-assisted maintenance workflows.

faq.question: Does it modify repositories by default?
faq.answer: Some documented commands are read-only, but sync, apply, prune, push, and release workflows can modify repositories.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes Claude Code sessions managed directly or through ntm robot mode.

faq.question: Can it process dirty repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. The agent-sweep workflow can plan, commit, and optionally release changes after preflight checks.

faq.question: What are the main security concerns?
faq.answer: The main concerns are remote install scripts, repository write operations, credential handling, and automated agent commits.

faq.question: Is this a complete CLI implementation?
faq.answer: No. This skill provides operational guidance for an external CLI rather than the full source code.
